strings.NTG_CountryInfo_Content_desc.1:
Throughout the tenure of Premier Nikolai Bukharin, a visionary scheme, dubbed the Siberian Plan was created to develop a highly mechanized industrial heart within the deep confines of the Soviet Union, far from possible invaders while simultaneously developing formerly unconnected regions.

Under this ambitious plan, factories, industrial lines and mines that were built up in Siberia gave Krasnoyarsk the helping push to develop into a big industrial centre, much like its fellow sibling cities of Tomsk and Novosibirsk.

Due to the expansive size of the Soviet Union, the far region of Siberia allowed for opposition against Bukharin to grow. Political dissidents formally dismissed by the premier swelled in popularity amongst a complacent population.
strings.NTG_CountryInfo_Content_desc.2:
As Nikolai Bukharin solidified his control over the Soviet Union, two of Vladimir Lenin’s protégés would be sidelined. One being Joseph Stalin, and the other, was none other than Lev Davidovich Bronstein, more popularly known as Leon Trotsky. As a central instigator of the Bolshevik Revolutions of the 1910s, Trotsky would rise to become amongst one of the few men at the top of Soviet leadership.

Despite his loss to succeed Lenin as Premier, Trotsky would mark his faction within the Bolshevik Party, with the Left Opposition. Forming just after the death of Lenin, Trotsky would find himself firm friends amongst members of higher echelons in the army, people's commissars and Old Bolsheviks.

Distrustful of Bukharin’s legitimacy as Lenin’s successor this coalition of disgruntled polities eventually signed the Declaration of 45, a document decrying against the bureaucratic cliques forming in the halls of the Moscow Soviet and Presidium, an attack aimed directly at Bukharin.
strings.NTG_CountryInfo_Content_desc.3:
While Bukharin continued his crackdown on political dissent on other factions in the Bolshevik Party, Trotsky would repeatedly savagely criticize Bukharin's economic policies on industrialisation. He tore down every minute decision, every bill, every word that the Premier uttered, decrying his actions as weak, going as far as claiming that Bukharin had strayed too far from the path in which Lenin set out.

Unbeknownst to him, this would cost him his life. Later that year, an unknown assassin attacked him in his Irkutsk home, ending the revolutionary’s life prematurely, whilst his supporters would end up exiled, scattered throughout various posts in faraway lands.

Despite the loss of their main ideologue, Trotskyism survived, with its successors still prominent members active within the Bolshevik Party, bitter and burning within their hearts. Bukharin had won, purging all of his internal enemies out of sight. However, the Union would soon find itself in trouble.
strings.NTG_CountryInfo_Content_desc.4:
Operation Barbarossa would throw the entire Soviet Union into a self-destructive disarray. As the Wehrmacht overran settlement after settlement, it was soon clear that the end was inevitable. With many being evacuated towards the Urals, or abandoning their posts to join remnants of the Soviet Government in Siberia or the Far East, Bukharin’s union would finally disintegrate into pieces.

Trotskyism would become a quiet footnote within Soviet history, washed away by the backdrop of the collapse and destruction of the Soviet Union ...or so that’s what their opponents thought.
strings.NTG_CountryInfo_Content_desc.5:
Split into various splinter states across the former Soviet Union, many citizens fleeing from Bukharin’s failures, or the ever increasing suppression by the NKVD in the Far East would settle within the democratic Central Siberian Republic.

However, tensions would grow between the Republic and Remnants of the Soviet Presidium, with the Soviet Remnants declaring war against the fledgling Republic, culminating in the Siberian War.

What was expected to be a quick war, escalated into a regional one that resulted in the already fractured glass of Russia to be further shattered into fiefdoms, centered in various cities across the region. As the Army of Central Siberia broke up and became the personal armies of warlords, the people of Krasnoyarsk decided to take matters into their own hands.
strings.NTG_CountryInfo_Content_desc.6:
In the chaos of retreat and consolidation, military bases, weapons caches and ammunition points were left abandoned by both sides, with many still containing serviceable arms for further use.

With no one to guard them, and no protection from any organized government, many villages and towns would enter such munition points and arm themselves with these leftovers from the Siberian armies, sustained themselves through hunting, and if necessary, fended off against the big bands of raiders and bandits.

And so formed the various militias in the suburbs of Krasnoyarsk, who frequently patrolled and protected their own property, becoming a recognizable sign of the region, where refugees entered and left without loss of life.
strings.NTG_CountryInfo_Content_desc.7:
In the wake of withdrawal by both sides, a problem of governance arose. The city was losing its power supply, and soon a slow death became commonplace.

The Trotskyists rose up and organized themselves, forming a local government. With the massive support of exiles, his father’s followers and former Bolshevik members within the city, taking control was only a menial task.

Although nominally loyal to the Central Siberian Republic, General Nikolai Andreev and his officers' clique would see where the wind was blowing. Although wishing to rule the city, he would lend his support to the Trotskyists, ending up in the General Staff of the reformed Red Army.

For now, Russia’s only a bastion of Trotskyism lies in Krasnoyarsk, but only time will tell if the lowly statelet will reignite the fire of revolution, restore the Motherland, and bring the workers’ revolution to the world.
strings.NTG_THENEWORDER_DESC:
As the Soviet Union decayed and broke into its many different warlord states, Nizhny Tagil seemed to be roughly untouched by the various conflicts that surrounded its landscape. During the war against the Fascist invaders, the industry that was built up in Western Siberia let Nizhny Tagil develop into a big industrial centre, much like its fellow cities of Sverdlovsk and Tyumen, allowing for arsenals to arm it’s civilian militias against the many bandits that roamed the vast wastes.

These militias became an iconic part of Nizhny Tagil’s identity, as the Anarchy years loomed further in.

Due to the distance from Tyumen, and the Far East led by Yagoda, Nizhny Tagil became a calling hub for many people to seek refuge, especially former political prisoners that were set free in the rapid collapse of the Soviet Union. These prisoners, sent to the gulags by Yagoda, escaped and in turn led by Lev Sedov, formed the Trotskyist Government of Nizhny Tagil.

Despite the tense reception of the civilian populace against this new form of government, many begrudgingly accept this new state of affairs, for their promises could lead to a better tomorrow for them, but not everyone is keen on supporting Sedov’s policies.
strings.NTG_regional_unifier_communist_DEF: the West Siberian Soviet Socialist Republic
strings.NTG_RUS_communist_DEF: the Union of Soviet Socialist Republics
strings.NTG_bastion_of_the_revolution_desc: Nizhny Tagil, before the Great Patriotic War, was a centre of opposition to Bukharin and his supporters. Nizhny Tagil was also a home to many revolutionary organizations. Today, Nizhny Tagil remains the bastion of the Russian Revolution and a symbol of the struggle for social justice and equality. Despite the passage of time and the many changes that have taken place in Russia since the early years of the revolution, Nizhny Tagil remains a powerful reminder of the enduring importance of the ideals and values of the revolution.
strings.NTG_satirical_pamphlets_desc: An unknown author has been writing and distributing satirical anti-communist pamphlets in the region. Spreading amidst the many smaller organized armed groups these pamphlets continue to further undermine our attempts to liberate the workers of Russia.
strings.NTG_widespread_armaments_desc: Due to abandonment of weapons depots due to the Anarchy that befell us, many villages and citizens in Nizhny Tagil are armed and organised into local neighbourhood watches and militias to ward off bandits. Whilst this isn't a problem yet, the Red Army nor the local Party does not have direct control of these men with guns, which could severely hamper the monopoly over violence of Nizhny Tagil's rulers.
strings.NTG_collectivised_farms_desc:
With the recent uptick in voluntary collectivization of farms, we have received word that agricultural output has increased, with grain output slowly increasing, we can now authorise a greater amount of rations for our loyal workers and soldiers.

Whilst there are some delegates who disagree with where the excess agricultural output should be going towards, we now can relax in relative calm, knowing that we will not starve in Nizhny Tagil.
strings.NTG_subsidized_war_industries_desc:
Lowing many years of pleading from the Revolutionary Military Council to the Presidium, along with the increasing specter of looming war on the horizon, we have granted new investments into the armed forces and military production.

These investments are predicted to increase the capabilities of our armed forces as well as our future preparedness for the wars against our neighboring warlords. This has been a great boost to our Red Army and potentially grant us victory in the coming war.
strings.NTG_novaja_ekonomiceskaja_politika_desc: Sinyavsky’s “Return to NEP” is a massive success. The implementation of the policy has allowed for greater funds for our nation to spend on essential services and formerly neglected governmental sectors as well as increase the quality of life in our nation, with our citizens able to afford their daily bread without much difficulty.
strings.NTG_Karl_Radek_hog_desc:
Chairman of the Council of People's Commissars
Trotskyism
--------------
Born in Lemberg on October 31, 1885, Karl Radek was deeply involved in the Communist movement from an early age.

Radek became active in the Communist movement in Poland and Germany before meeting Vladimir Lenin. He played a key role in the February and October Revolutions, helping Lenin and the communists return to Russia, establish the Russian Soviet Federative Socialist Republic, and form the Communist Party of Germany, as well as plan the Spartacist Rebellion.

The inter-war period was turbulent for Radek. Expelled from the party in 1927 for organizing a movement on the 10th Anniversary of the Revolution, he was exiled to Tomsk.

He was readmitted to the Party in 1930 but faced trouble due to his favorable comments on the National Socialist government in Germany when the Germans invaded the Union in 1941. Imprisoned for his German sympathies, Radek spent eight years in a labor camp in Verkhneuralsk. As the Union collapsed, he escaped to Tomsk and then Nizhny Tagil.

Now an older man, Radek is determined to support Sedov’s revolution to atone for his past mistakes.
strings.NTG_Leonid_Serebryakov_for_desc:
People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs
Trotskyism
--------------
Leonid Serebryakov was born in Samara on June 11, 1890. Coming from a working-class family, he left home to work in a metal plant in Ufa, where he joined the underground socialist movement and participated in the failed 1905 revolution.

After being arrested and exiled for two years, he returned as a delegate at the Prague Conference in 1912, meeting Vladimir Lenin. Back in his hometown, he faced several arrests before being drafted into the Imperial Russian Army.

His revolutionary activities gained fame while stationed in Kostroma, where he led his unit in support of the February Revolution, aiding the Bolsheviks in establishing the Kostroma Soviet. Rising through the Communist Party ranks, he became a party organizer in Moscow by 1917 and a Secretariat member of the Central Committee by 1919. During the Civil War, he served on the Southern Front with Joseph Stalin and became Deputy Commissar for Transport in 1924.

A member of the Left Opposition, he supported Trotsky and held a significant role as head of the Central Administration of Highways and Automobile Transport. In 1936, he was ousted under false charges and exiled but returned to the party before WWII. During the war, he organized infrastructure and transport for the Red Army.

As Stalin purged disloyal members, Serebryakov fled to Nizhny Tagil, living quietly until approached by former comrade Yevgeny Preobrazhensky to help reestablish a Soviet Society. With nothing left to lose, he accepted and loyally served the revolution once more.
strings.NTG_Yevgeni_Preobrazhensky_eco_desc:
People's Commissar for Finance
Trotskyism
--------------
Yevgeni Preobrazhensky was born on February 15, 1886, in Bolkhov, Oryol. Coming from an Orthodox Archpriest’s family, he attended a parochial school and later the Gymnasium, where he rejected religion and became involved in socialist activities.

He joined the Russian Social Democratic Labor Party and played a significant role in the 1905 revolution, leading student rallies and labor strikes in Oryol. After multiple arrests, he was exiled to Siberia but escaped and organized for the Bolsheviks.

During the February Revolution, Preobrazhensky participated in the East Siberian Congress of Soviets and was elected to the First All-Russian Congress of Soviets of Workers' and Soldiers' Deputies. He served as Secretariat of the Central Committee before resigning to join the People’s Commissariat of Finance, where he criticized Bukharin’s policies and took part in a 1927 independent movement.

Expelled from the party, he was later reinstated and held significant roles, including a position with the People’s Commissariat of Light Industry and as acting head of the People’s Commissariat of State Farms. In 1937, he was ousted by Bukharin’s allies and sent to the Urals.

Preobrazhensky oversaw growth in the Urals until the Union's collapse. He then fled to Irkutsk, where he criticized Stalin’s policies. As Yagoda cracked down on dissent, he escaped to Nizhny Tagil. Upon Sedov’s declaration of the new commune of Nizhny Tagil, he joined, continuing his revolutionary work despite his age.
strings.NTG_Vladimir_Antonov_Ovseenko_sec_desc:
People's Commissar for Military Affairs
Trotskyism
--------------
Vladimir Antonov-Ovseenko was born on March 9, 1883, in Chernigov, to a nobleman and a military officer. After graduating from the Voronezh Cadet Corps in 1901, he was expelled from Military Engineering School for refusing to swear allegiance to the Tsar.

He enrolled in the St. Petersburg Infantry School in 1902, where he became active in the underground socialist movement. As a 2nd Lieutenant, he was arrested multiple times for his role in the 1905 Revolution and subsequent uprisings before fleeing Russia and meeting Leon Trotsky in France in 1914. During the 1917 Revolutions, he joined the Bolsheviks, participating in key events like the storming of the Winter Palace and commanding the Ukrainian and Southern Fronts during the Russian Civil War.

After the civil war, Antonov-Ovseenko was sidelined by Bukharin and his allies due to his support for Trotsky. Threatening a coup if Bukharin harmed Trotsky, he became a pariah among Bukharinists. He was sent on diplomatic missions, advising the Spanish Republicans in 1936 before being recalled and relegated to a low-level post.

Exiled by Stalin, he escaped from a prison train and ended up in Nizhny Tagil. There, he quietly organized a socialist movement and supported Lev Sedov's new commune by organizing a new Red Army. Despite his age, Antonov-Ovseenko remains ready to fight for the revolution.
strings.NTG_Valram_Shalamov_hog_desc:
Chairman of the Council of Peoples Commissars
Trotskyism
--------------
Valram Tikhonovich Shalamov was born on June 16, 1907, in Vologda, Russia, and spent much of his early life in Butugychag, Kolyma, Siberia. The son of a priest, he worked his way up through the communist system and eventually joined the Soviet Law faculty at Moscow University, where he engaged in discussions and critiques of Bukharin’s policies.

Shalamov was arrested and sent to a work camp in the Northern Urals. Although released in 1932, he was arrested again in 1937 on charges of anti-Soviet agitation, which radically shifted his views. He was sent to Kolyma, where he received a five-year sentence extended to ten years. As the Soviet Union collapsed, he was released due to the deteriorating war situation.

Fearing Yagoda’s NKVD State and wanting to avoid the Central Siberian War, Shalamov fled to Tomsk. When the Republic began to collapse and splinter, he moved to Nizhny Tagil, where he encountered Sedov’s revolution.

Determined to protect himself and ensure the survival of Trotsky’s ideals amid the chaos, Shalamov chose to join Sedov’s cause.
strings.NTG_Yury_Dombrovsky_for_desc:
People's Commissar for Foreign Affairs
Trotskyism
--------------
Yury Osipovich Dombrovsky was born on February 2, 1909, in Moscow. Raised in a family of intellectuals, he was immersed in literature and philosophy from a young age, developing a deep love for learning and the written word. As a youth, Dombrovsky was an enthusiastic member of the Communist Party, holding various positions within the organization.

However, he grew disillusioned with the party’s increasing suppression of artistic and intellectual freedom. After the collapse of the Soviet Union, he escaped with Marshal Vasilevsky and the remnants of the Soviet Army, enduring harsh weather and bandits before arriving in Nizhny Tagil.

Despite his near brush with death, Dombrovsky continued writing and published his magnum opus, “The Faculty of Useless Knowledge,” in 1955. The novel, a profound exploration of the human condition, art, philosophy, and politics, also served as a critique of the Soviet regime’s censorship and repression following Stalin’s coup.

After the revolution in Nizhny Tagil, Dombrovsky chose to join Sedov, sharing the common goal of rescuing Russia from oppression.
strings.NTG_Alexander_Alexeyev_sec_desc:
People's Commissar for Military Affairs
Trotskyism
--------------
Alexander Ivanovich Alexeyev was born on August 14, 1913, in Kostroma. After losing his father at 16, he moved to Moscow to follow his older brother and graduated in 1935. He then enrolled in the history department at Moscow University. In 1939, Alexeyev was sent to Spain as an interpreter for Soviet Military Specialists and was soon recruited into the NKVD.

By late 1941, he was posted to Iran but was quickly recalled to support the military effort against the Germans. Attached to the NKVD, he was sent to Yagoda's Far East. Disillusioned with Yagoda's regime while serving as a commissar with a Red Army unit, Alexeyev seized the chance to escape to Nizhny Tagil as the Central Siberian War stalled. There, he joined Vladimir Antonov-Ovseenko.

Despite lacking formal military experience, Alexeyev's skills as an interpreter and his NKVD background made him a crucial asset in Lev Sedov's revolution in Nizhny Tagil. Now, he is prepared to use his expertise to support Sedov’s efforts to restore the Union.
strings.NTG_memories_of_the_father_desc: It is necessary to look back and remember our old leader, Leon Trotsky, the guiding hand and founder of our glorious movement. Everything our state is based on has lept from his mind. Though he left this world nearly a decade ago, his face still stands proud on posters and flags. Most importantly, his son, our glorious chairman, remembers as well.
strings.NTG_remember_the_past_desc: The early days of the Soviet Union were a wonderful era. A time of hopes and dreams, during which many revolutionary ideas appeared. At the same time, Leon Trotsky began his activity. Even if in the end it resulted in the deformation of the working state and the collapse of Russia, we should not forget about this era. After all, there is no future without the past.
strings.NTG_reflect_on_the_present_desc: And where are we now? A snow-covered wasteland in the middle of which there are several divided cities. Russia is destroyed, but life goes on. Maybe the situation seems hopeless, but life goes on. Maybe someday this will change.
strings.NTG_look_to_the_future_desc:
The future looks hazy. But while we are fighting, while our hearts are beating, the idea of a free and honest Russia will not die! And if we can achieve our goal, the whole world will see the willpower of the proletariat and the dreams of a world revolution will become even closer to reality!“ 

 ### 6.2 - PRE-SMUTA FOCI ###
strings.NTG_the_legacy_of_trotskyism_desc:
It is necessary to look back and remember our old leader, Leon Trotsky, the guiding hand and founder of our glorious movement. Everything our state is based on his ideals and teachings. However, we are not alone in the Siberian woods.

Nizhny Tagil is an enclave, being surrounded by the likes of Corporatist-Capitalists in Novosibirsk and the mad king’s court in Kemerovo, the bandits who live in Kansk and the remnants of the Central Siberian Republic in Tomsk, armed, against us and our ideals for the Siberian worker.

The future of the revolution seems bleak, yet, we will not back down from this challenge. We will show the world that we will survive and spread Trotsky’s dream across the Siberian Plains and later, the whole of Russia!
strings.NTG_vanguard_of_the_revolution_desc:
Premier Lev Sedov has lived a hard life, from seeing his father's work destroyed by false revolutionaries and seeing his motherland decimated in the War of 1941.

However, he has not let that stop him, as he stands as the vanguard of Trotsky's ideas, infused with Lenin and Marx's teachings. Continuing in their footsteps, unlike the false revolutionaries who reside in Tyumen and Irkutsk.

Trotsky and his ideals, with Lenin’s vision, led to the Union’s formation and victory in 1922. His military cunning formed the Red Army, which served with distinction and sacrifice during the War, his policies half-implemented led the working class to greater heights and greater prosperity.

Lev Sedov will continue his father’s legacy, following the philosophies of the Revolution, and pushing them forward into this uncertain age. For the vanguard does not falter.
strings.NTG_in_his_name_desc:
The line of Bolshevik succession from the very start was plain and simple; Lenin’s successor would be Trotsky. Afterall, how could the Red Prince of the Revolution not be the destined successor of Lenin in his quest for international communism.

However, due to counter-revolutionary cells and corrupt deals, Nikolai Bukharin managed to blind Lenin with his masked reactionary thoughts, securing the premiership and banishing Trotsky from his rightful place, before Stalin’s coup against the Union, ensuring the decades of disaster that would plague the Union and its people.

It is now our duty to bring about the rise of Trotsky's ideas, to restore the idea of the permanent revolution for all of the oppressed peoples to participate in. Lev Sedov, Trotsky's protege, will usher in this new age with himself at the mantle of the new revolution.

In our revolutionary quest, the enslaved victims of capitalism and fascism shall be freed, the Motherland will be reunited once again under the red banner, and history will be faithfully rectified once and for all.
strings.NTG_denounce_the_false_revolutionaries_d:
It is time we address an important question. The False Revolutionaries who still influence our socialist thinking and creating schism in a united revolutionary thought.

Bukharin’s thinking, flawed in implementation, yet he was the reason why the Union recovered from the struggle in the reconstruction years. However, he must shoulder some blame for the mismanagement of the war in its early years.

Stalin, the traitor with his clique, who ousted and backstabbed his way to get to the top, sabotaging our war effort and the army’s brave soldiers. He nailed the coffin for our Union.

Sedov has decided to seize the opportunity to address this at the Annual Party Meeting, to denounce the traitor to the revolution, and to rehabilitate Bukharin’s standing.

Maybe, with this, we can finally mend the schism and forge a better future.“
strings.NTG_stalin_sins_desc:
Joseph Stalin. The biggest false revolutionary of them all.

He rubbed shoulders with the other Old Bolsheviks during the Civil War. Hailed as a hero, and was part of the 3 potential successors to succeed Lenin. How foolish had we been.

During the crisis that befell us during Operation Barbarossa, he backstabbed us through a coup, cracking down on loyalists who voiced out the criticism of the entire farce. When the West Russian Front stagnated under his rule, he ran to his fiefdom instead, abandoning our citizens in the occupied lands to their fate.

He is the murderer of the Union, who incited the fragmentation of Russia, and the biggest traitor to the Soviet People. Stalin and his faction will be branded as outlaws, and purged from the Party’s history.
strings.NTG_show_mercy_to_bukharinists_desc:
Nikolai Bukharin remains a name vilified by many of the Presidium and our delegates. Yet we must realise, Bukharin’s policies have benefitted us more than we’d like to think.

His Siberian Plan has provided places such as Nizhny Tagil an opportunity to grow and develop industrially before its tragic demise. Additionally, despite all his flaws and the mismanagement, he managed to ensure our citizens had a better quality of life than under the Tsar and his siloviki.

We should give mercy to them, they were blinded by ambition and their goals. This is the only way to heal the fracture amongst like-minded revolutionaries and restore our Union on the global stage.
strings.NTG_the_party_of_the_people_desc:
We have always been the party of the people.

In all things in our state, aspects of life and our socialist society lie with the party. The party which has provided the people with security, provided them with the ability to grow on land where violence and chaos has plagued it for years.

The party has aimed to give every citizen a roof over their head, food and water, proper social services, education, and gainful employment. In return, the people assist us in our day to day activities and play a part in our society, by providing to our state.

Without the party we would be nothing, descending back into madness and anarchy. Without the people, we would be another prey for the fascists and capitalists of the world. We have made this mistake once, and we will never allow them to take advantage of it ever again.

Truly, for the people, by the people.
strings.NTG_the_issue_of_militias_desc:
As the whole of Russia collapsed into anarchy, and the civilian government in Nizhny Tagil reorganized amidst the last days of the Central Siberian War, the military abandoned arms depots and military bases, leaving the citizens with their valuable weapons.

These allowed the formation of volunteer militia units, who armed themselves with such weapons to defend against the bandits and roaming gangs that dared loot and pillage in the Siberian Wastes.

Lately however, the situation has stabilized and our army has been established, protecting our borders. Yet the militias remain, rivaling our army’s dominance of power in our fledgling workers’ state as well as questioning our right to rule. This raises the question... how should we solve this problem?
strings.NTG_an_olive_branch_desc:
These militias have served the people well, regardless of their ideological standing. These men have been essential to our society and army, especially since the Anarchy years, protecting our current lands whilst we reorganized our army.

Willing militia units have offered to join, train and give up their arms for our soldiers, giving our men valuable experience. Additionally, they assist policing and governance, helping fill in the deficiencies in our administrative systems.

They have proven their worth thus far. We shall allow them to keep their rights to exist temporarily, before integration at a later date.
strings.NTG_reform_the_red_army_desc:
Our Army in Nizhny Tagil is woefully underequipped.

Some units are at half strength, others armed with rifles older than their fathers, a few have only shovels. Our situation is gravely problematic However, the situation is not as bleak as we thought.

Some like-minded militias, recently granted their legal status and benefits, have decided to turn in surplus equipment and inform us about abandoned caches and military bases, left in the vast plains.

Our industry, which has survived the chaos and destruction, has been restarted, with workers producing new military equipment for our brave soldiers. New equipment has started to slowly trickle in.
strings.NTG_no_compromises_desc:
If we wish to maintain the strength, independence, and fortitude of our Red Army, we cannot stray off of the path of Trotskyism whatsoever. Not an inch must be ceded to the opposition if we wish to achieve total military autonomy and strength.

If we adapt these counter-revolutionary reforms to our military and militias, the consequences will haunt us for years to come, it will be an echo of the catastrophe our forces suffered in the first Great Patriotic War.

No, we will stick with the objectively correct path, the way of Trotsky. Sedov will ensure it will not be tarnished in any way shape or form. It is paramount that we forbid any vast reform to our military administration unless strictly necessary, to secure our commune’s defense and offensive capabilities.
strings.NTG_stay_true_to_our_ideas_desc:
These military reforms proposed by some members of the Presidium are absurd, inefficient, and in some cases even counter-revolutionary against our ideals.

The militias have been a problematic spot, even if a majority have decided to work with us.

More importantly, we must not stray off of the values of the Red Army that Trotsky intended for us to follow. Let us not forget the way he valiantly led his troops in his steel train, bringing freedom, socialism, and liberty along with him as he vanquished the Tsarist forces all the way back to the pacific.

Lev Sedov will maintain the orthodox doctrine of the Red Army and Red Guard militias, guaranteeing the commune’s national security and further building the foundations for the imminent permanent revolution.

We will stay true to our vision.
strings.NTG_the_most_important_day_desc:
The future is here.

A bastion of Trotskyism, standing in Central Siberia. Stronger than ever.

Our reforms to organize an effective Red Army, a working political system based on the ideas of Karl Marx and Leon Trotsky, establishment of a peasants' democracy, and a collectivized economy, have paid off.

Our working class no longer needs to worry about slave-like working hours and wages, and the average Farmer does not need to worry about their daily bread or starve the nation. This is a great achievement.

However, spring is arriving. Rumours have spread of the other warlords planning to attack each other. Many are scared and worried for war and grief to spread across the plains once more.

Yet, the Red Army stands to defend ourselves, our workers supporting them in the industries, our farmers growing crops to feed our populace.

Trotsky's flame ignites their hearts anew, liberation dawns. Destiny's blessing has begun.
strings.NTG_the_moderate_bourgeoisie_question_de:
One of the core principles of the original testaments of Lenin was the complete and utter elimination of the upper class elites, the main proponents of capitalist oppression and tyrannical murder. So far, we have been successful in our endeavors, with these influences being rooted out wherever our red banner flew, yet now we face a new dilemma pertaining to these edicts.

Throughout the past decade, the economic and social anarchy which has plagued the motherland has led to a new class of ‘moderate bourgeoisie’ to arise, mainly stemming from neo-kulaks and ambitious factory heads. Our principles prioritize the eradication of these proponents of inequality, yet an elimination on this level would remove much of the intelligentsia that resides within the commune, as well as loyal Union supporters.

The Presidium shall decide on this, with careful consideration.
strings.NTG_exile_the_hardliners_desc:
As we dive deeper into the ideological loyalties of the Russian people, we find something sinister that has risen in the Anarchy.

Societies run by Monarchists, Fascists and Nazis, who hide from the shadows, plotting their coup against us. Believing in the same ideology that enslaved and destroyed the foundations of our nation, they pose the biggest threat to us than the ideological differences between fellow socialists.

We will thus begin to crack down on them, and exile them from our worker’s state. The intelligence service will find them out and send them to meet their justice. These hardliners and reactionaries have no place in our society, and they will be stamped out.

These monarchists and fascists, will be sent to labor camps or thrown into the Siberian wastes, where they will serve the workers state by redemption or feed the wolves.
strings.NTG_form_a_bolshevik_democracy_desc:
Throughout our campaigns of revolutionary activity and anti-fascist action, we have always done our best to cradle and keep paramount the ideals of democracy. Unfortunately, time and time again, reactionary elements have infiltrated the ballot boxes ever since the first election in 1918. From this, and the numerous sham democracies plastered across the west, we have developed a new method of democracy, one that would preserve the people's freedom in national decision making as well as keep out the decadence of capitalism and totalitarianism.

Bolshevik Democracy, known by others as Soviet Democracy, is the practice of fully democratic elections under the supervision and protection of the communist state, a policy that we shall take to heart alongside Trotskyism. Besides, how can we have a fully sustainable revolution without the will of the people?

This method of safe-guarded democracy is, on paper, meant to be only temporary, a provisional system meant for the inevitable transition towards a fully free and unrestrained socialist democracy. It is our duty to ensure that this bright future will be secured for our future generations and society as a whole.
strings.NTG_our_path_finally_secured_desc:
We have come a long way on our path here in this small enclave. Our recent reforms with our Army, the reshaping of the political landscape and mending the schisms in the party have finally borne fruit.

Our workers, who didn’t have a voice in the factories, now can form worker’s councils and have a direct line for change and reform. Our farmers, who toiled to harvest grain, can rest easy knowing they can seek help from us should crops fail or machines break.

They will never have to suffer needlessly again to serve the people.

Our Soldiers, now ready and armed, will protect the nation, and liberate the oppressed workers across the shattered Russian landscape and, eventually to our currently occupied lands under the Nazi jackboot, bringing the Revolution with them.

We have secured our path in Nizhny Tagil today. Tomorrow, we will secure it in Siberia, and later, we will secure it in Moscow, Minsk, Kiev and Smolensk.
strings.NTG_crush_the_reactionaries_desc:
Reactionaries are a dangerous threat to us, much more dangerous than the enemies that surround us.

They hide in plain sight, which makes it the most difficult. Most of them challenge us to maintain a status-quo, where we, the workers, are still oppressed and subjugated by the vile capitalists, working for their profit, rather than ours

Others are more extreme, asking for the return of a monarch and the right to absolute authority, or looking for a system similar to the fascists.

These people are not tolerated in our society, and it is our duty to stomp them out and erase their vile, oppressive and hateful speech from our society.
strings.NTG_the_foundations_of_the_red_army: The Foundations of the Red Army
strings.NTG_the_foundations_of_the_red_army_desc:
The Red Army was once united, bringing down the corrupted regime of Alexander Kerensky, during the October Revolution. Led by Leon Trotsky, it became a strong force to be reckoned with in the East.

It would be mutilated by the political backstabbing in the party and shattered beyond recognition during the war. The Red Army split into various warlords, with many having no interest in defending the people.

Our Army in Nizhny Tagil may claim to be a legitimate successor to the Red Army, yet it is made up with eager volunteers and desperadoes, armed with weapons older than them.

There is no motivation for our soldiers to fight, whilst our officers do not have initiative to learn nor innovate new tactics. There is a shortage of men willing to serve our state and no set goal for our Red Army.

It seems, we need to lay the foundations of the Red Army once more.
strings.NTG_employ_an_offensive_doctrine_desc:
Now that we have rebuilt the foundations of the Red Army, we must choose a doctrine for the coming conflict.

Despite some calls from the generals to focus on defense, Premier Sedov and Alexeyev have decided that an offensive doctrine would benefit us in the long run. From our bases in Nizhny Tagil, we will strike using speed and shock to our advantage, overrunning our enemies before they have time to react.

After all, the best defense is a good offense.
strings.NTG_start_the_draft_desc:
If we are ever to overwhelm and surpass the military might of our hostile neighbors, we must ratify and implement conscription. This is a necessity, for our Red Army is no match in size for some of the armies of Siberia.

To solve this problem, Deputy Commissar Alexeyev has drawn up plans for a reserve force of conscripts. This will fill the ranks of the Red Army.

This will allow us to implement a broad use of conscription, which will be implemented and relaxed according to the needs of the nation. This will definitely strengthen our ranks as we prepare for a possible war with our neighbors.

However, we must not get carried away with conscripting everyone. Conscripted personnel means fewer workers in the factories and fewer farm hands in the fields, which could negatively affect our nation in a time of war.
strings.NTG_fight_for_the_revolution_desc:
The Predecessors of the Red Army proved themselves when they overthrew the regime of Alexander Kerensky, storming the Winter Palace and driving the foreigners out of our motherland.

Our late leader Leon Trotsky organized the Red Army of Workers and Peasants into one of the best fighting forces in the Eastern sphere of the globe, fighting for the people enslaved by the capitalists, breaking their chains and setting them free.

From then on, the Red Army fought for everything and everyone. For their homes, their families, their comrades, for the motherland. It is no different today. The principles of the Red Army are simple: to defend our workers and to liberate the enslaved workers in our vast motherland.

We are fighting for everything, for our right to survive.
strings.NTG_the_military_science_committee_desc:
The military and the field of science have long been intertwined. Science has allowed the innovation of new equipment, tactics and discoveries which assist the army in reforming and revitalising itself to go toe-to-toe with its enemies.

In Nizhny Tagil, this is no different. Many technical experts have offered their services to the army on an ad-hoc basis, innovating on weapons design and newer methods to improve equipment reliability. The army has long petitioned to recognise their work, whilst assisting the technical experts by offering desperately needed funds for their scientific projects.

We shall formalise this process by establishing the Military Science Committee, allowing our officers and technical experts to work jointly, reducing the time wasted for technical experts to approach our army for innovative solutions.
strings.NTG_subsidize_war_industries_desc:
As we begin to plan for the liberation of our region, we will need to begin the production of much needed weapons, but we will not be able to produce enough if we do not subsidize the loss of civilian production for weapons and ammunition.

So far, our economic plans have focused primarily on our civilian industries, allowing for the growth of our economy and a better standard of living for our citizens, but due to the dangerous situation, we must divert production to weapons and uniforms, subsidizing the military industries.

It may hurt economic growth in the short term, but it will be necessary for our continued survival and eventual pursuit of the reunification of our nation before funding the Permanent Revolution globally.
strings.NTG_modernize_our_troops_desc:
Historically, the army with the technological advantage has always won the battles.

Even today, this rings true, without better weapons and equipment, we would be easily be swept away the other enemies that surround us, letting them seize the opportunity to return our Motherland to their reactionary and degenerate ideals.

We must quickly redouble our efforts to modernize our troops, replacing bolt actions rifles with automatic rifles, and replacing old uniforms with newer ones. This way, our troops will stand a chance against the enemies of the Permanent Revolution.
strings.NTG_gather_old_military_plans_desc:
Recently, in a repurposed military base, our soldiers found important documents stamped with old STAVKA emblems. These documents were passed up the chain of command and are now on the desks of our generals.

In them are the war plans of the Western Russian War and of the Great Patriotic War. Although they are not fully applicable to us, it seems that our general staff can learn from their plans and tactics and implement them in our strategy for prosecuting the next war.

By learning from them, new plans can be drawn up and used in various scenarios that apply to us. This would give us an advantage that could be used against our enemies, as well as a much needed lesson for our generals who have not had the opportunity to learn from their predecessors.
strings.NTG_a_red_sky_desc:
With our crushing defeat in the Great Patriotic War and the failure of the West Russian Offensive, we have learnt much from our foes.

One of these lessons was the importance of having a capable air force. A well equipped, well trained and modern air force that can contest air superiority, that can support our attacking troops and protect our skies have a combat advantage, potentially changing the tide of battle and a conflict as a whole.

That said, our surveyors have found an abandoned air base that was formerly used for the maintenance of the Central Siberian Air Force. Hopefully, we can repurpose the facility and re-establish the Soviet Air Force, giving us an advantage against our nearest enemies and potentially contest the Falcon’s domain.
strings.NTG_a_red_land_desc:
Motorization has been always a priority for the Red Army, ever since we produced our own domestically built trucks. Starting in the first decade after the civil war, we built motorised units of our own.

Despite our defeat against the Germans in West Russia, we learnt more than ever before. Motorised Divisions, well armed and equipped, allowed ourselves the speed and power necessary to break through the lines of fascist defenses, liberating vast swathes of occupied territory.

We shall do the same here and now, building our own motorised divisions to overrun our enemies and destroy them before they have a chance to organise an attack. Speed and Power saves lives.
strings.NTG_expand_industrial_capacity_desc:
The Siberian Plan envisioned by Premier Bukharin was intended to make Siberia an industrious location, in the heart of the motherland, bringing new economic and employment opportunities in the plains.

Now, the industries lay idle, the economies of Siberia stagnating or hardly prosperous, with states having to raid others to survive the wastes. Machinery has been left rusted, derelict or broken down for scrap.

In light of the situation, the Party has already declared that it has planned to revitalise the industries and the economy through economic planning and investment, and hopefully expand the industrial capacity of our nation.
strings.NTG_preobrazhensky_economic_plan_desc:
Although Sedov's plan is the proper path of Socialism, we must be wary of public opinion and the instability inflicted upon us by our neighbors. We will therefore begin to dial back on our war communist policies. The military will still be formidable and well-funded, but we will need to make way for monetary funds to reach our civilian economy instead of being thrown into a cesspit of unneeded spending.

Along with this, Lev Sedov has announced two things:
First, the Formation of the State Planning Committee, or the Gosplan. This agency will oversee our economic statistics, and prepare economic plans and advise for the Permanent Revolution.

Secondly, he has announced the start of the Five-Year Plan. This will see us abolishing our slug-like pace of nationalizing and centralizing the economy, and instead allowing for the NKVD, under Alexander Beloborodov, to begin enforcing these policies.
The Five-year Plan will also see the collectivization of all farming settlements in Russia, however not as rapidly as the nationalization of our Industries. This will assure that our peasants and farmers will have enough time to prepare and get themselves suited for living together.
We will also establish the Tolkach, which will cooperate with our Trade Unions to force the People's Commissars of State Industries to meet their quotas and standards, or else face removal.
We will thus formally switch over to a planned economy, where the state will be able to intervene at any moment should inflation rise, or the economy fall.
strings.NTG_nikolaevschina_desc:
An alternative proposal has been proposed by another cadre. Nikolay Nikolayevich Inozemtsev, in his proposal to the Presidium, has asked for reforms to the planned economy, with lesser state intervention and more independent market reform to allow for the recovery of the shattered economy, whilst maintaining more benefits for the workers through state intervention and establishment of worker’s brigades.

It has sounded good to the members of the party who have long proposed changes to the economy, to allow our workers a better quality of life and employment without big state intervention. However, they have noted that too many of his reforms may throw us over to become false revolutionaries.

Looking past this, Inozemtsev has been an established revolutionary, serving in the Red Army during the Great Patriotic War, however he has little to no experience in economics unlike Preobrazhensky and his aides, and we are unsure if these reforms may help us. However, we must try, if it helps us escape this quagmire we are in.
strings.NTG_collectivize_farms_desc:
As told by Marx, practiced by Lenin, and partially maintained by Bukharin, the economic strategy of state collectivization of national goods remains core to the principles of Trotskyism and communism in general. Comrade Sedov has not forgotten this priority, as shown by his recent propositions to the presidium, detailing a series of new collectivization efforts pertaining to the whole of the commune. This move, one showing rare support from both wings of the party, has been presented as another swift action against neo-kulaks and the bourgeois, yet there remain concerns.

The largest concern is the worry of food security, an issue made increasingly drastic by the Siberian collapse, which has led to the sharpest decline in agricultural outputs ever seen since the civil war. This concern is made even more apparent due to this year’s collectivization drive focusing on farms, with thousands of farmers set to be directly affected by these plans.

We must make sure that our future economic development plans maintain economic equality whilst keeping the commune away from famine.
strings.NTG_entact_the_welfare_programme_desc:
So far, the welfare program has been experimented on, reports have come in of more families who have been able to rise from poverty as a result of the welfare program.

After all, a better quality of life has always been a priority of ours, and workers who have healthy families that are well fed work harder in the factories.

However, we have noticed that there have been some downsides, with some workers choosing to use their welfare benefits on other unsavoury products, such as alcohol, or using their newly received money to gamble and misusing such handouts.

We shall have to reform the programme, handing out coupons and rations instead of giving straight handouts, allowing families to afford common products.
strings.NTG_distribute_goods_desc:
These economic plans, albeit having hurt some parts of our economy in the short run, has been a huge success! We can see our political enemies and Anti-Revolutionaries working in localized farming collectives, cut off from our mentally healthy farmers and workers. Due to our vast investments into the agricultural industry and collectivization being gradual to allow stockpiling of food, the process has been surprisingly swift and successful, with these collectives not only increasing our production in general but also our reforms have generated both popularity and a surplus of money, which will be given back to our workers.

The Gosplan is beginning to hand out large sums of “Social-Labour Pension” amongst our loyal farmers and workers, this has not only increased our popularity further, but it has also allowed for poverty to severely plummet throughout the population! Along with this, the surpluses of our food production and products such as cars, and even apartments, will be given to our working class, this will only further legitimize us as the only true successor of Karl Marx!

As a last gift from our generous Worker's State, we will begin giving out the remaining surplus to the unemployed and to jobs that don't include labor. We will also begin to construct apartment complexes for our impoverished people to live in. Lastly, the absolute leftovers may be given to these Bukharainists, Monarchists, and other traitors of the Worker State, if they can prove themselves to have abandoned the ideas of degenerates. they may be spared from these Gulags.
strings.NTG_reestablish_the_nep_desc:
So far, Inozemtsev’s policies have bore us much fruit.

By reducing the extensive state intervention in the economy, the people have greater economic freedoms to establish themselves in society. Additionally, through the establishment of the Welfare Programmes, many of our citizens have been able to climb out of poverty.

However, we have a big opposition towards his last policy, Re-establishing the New Economic Policy. Used by our late Premier Lenin to transition the shattered economy of our new Union. Trotsky did endorse it, believing the state should repossess all output to invest in capital formation and the transition to collective farming for our agriculture.

Now, Inozemtsev and independent cadres have proposed re-establishing the NEP, to rebuild the shattered economy and allow our people to have a greater quality of life. Many in the party feel strongly against the policy, however it is up to the Presidium to decide.
strings.NTG_a_crimson_renaissance_desc:
With our reforms in full swing, many have been worried about the results of rapid nationalization and our gradual collectivization, saying that we have either done too much or too little on these topics. We have, however, proved these Anti-Revolutionaries wrong.

We have never seen this much success before, the nationalization of the industries has allowed us to directly administer their quotas, standards, and size of investments. This has allowed us to keep up with the statistics of another reform, the Central Planning Committee or Gosplan, which has collaborated with the NKVD to provide us with accurate statistics. Our program of Workers' welfare and Social Pensions have been very popular amongst our working population. We have also distributed apartment complexes, and surpluses of our food and other goods for free or very little charge, thus evaporating widespread poverty!

The NKVD has also proved to be very helpful, in regard to finding saboteurs and Anti-Revolutionaries and sending them to Gulag Collectives. Collectivization has also been a great reform, especially with it being gradual. We have wiped out all isolated Obschina's and replaced them with State-Run farming communities-collectives. This has further allowed the Gosplan to better organize population censuses, production statistics, and subsequent economic growth. Our farms produce bread for the population, the population works in the factories, and the workers construct homes for the farmers and population. This is what Karl Marx and Leon Trotsky envisioned.

With the end of the Five Year Plan plan comes great success for our Worker's State, but this, as sadly predicted by the Gosplan, will not be enough to revive our economy in the long run. It should not be underestimated, it has brought great prosperity to our nation. But we need a more permanent solution for a permanent revolution.
strings.NTG_the_beginning_of_the_permanent_revol: The Beginning of the Permanent Revolution

After many months of rigorous reform of our economic policy, revitalization of our industrial capacity, and handling of the political front, the Presidium believes that we are ready to take on our enemies throughout the region.

Thus, we will begin our preparations for the unification of Central Siberia.

To begin with, we will have to concentrate on the warlords on our borders. We will begin to mobilize the Red Army and her reservists, drawing up plans to attack and conquer the surrounding states without much bloodshed, while temporarily reducing civilian production for the war industries in order to produce equipment for our soldiers.

Finally, we will make a radio broadcast to our old comrades, our veterans of the Great Patriotic War and the oppressed workers of Central Siberia, to join the revolutionary struggle and liberate themselves.

We will ask them to serve the Union in her most crucial hour!  With our reformed armed forces, superior technology and, finally, our stronger will, they will not stand a chance.

The Permanent Revolution has begun!
strings.NTG_lev_sedov_bizarre_adventures_desc:
Not long ago, it looked like Lev Sedov and the Trotskyists were just another tyrannical bunch living in the anarchy of Russia, spreading their dangerous ideas to the people of Siberia.

Nothing could have been further from the truth. Throughout his life, Sedov ventured around the world, from Europe to Asia Minor itself, spreading revolution. In the darkest days of the Soviet Union, he would quietly return and enter Yagoda's Republic before heading to Siberia. There he would begin to form the principles of a commune guided by his father's ideals.

Eventually, Sedov's hard work would pay off. When the Soviet Union collapsed, he would take advantage of it by contacting the remnants of the old Bolsheviks who had fled to Nizhny Tagil and forming the workers' state his father had always envisioned.

We have all come a long way since then, establishing our utopian democracy and a functioning state. But what would all this be for if we did not continue to spread our ideas and restore our Union to the workers' state it was.

Lev Sedov has witnessed many tragedies, personal conflicts and defeats, but this is a new adventure. An adventure that will see him realize his father's dreams, and possibly a better life for the people of Russia.
strings.NTG_prioritize_the_military_desc:
In times of war, sacrifices are made every day.

From the soldier in the field who dies for his nation, to the new conscript who sacrifices his civilian life to bear the burdens of being a soldier, to their families who see them off to war.

These men are defending the ideals of socialism! We must ensure that they receive the support and supplies they need to win this conflict and prevent the history of defeat from repeating itself.

This means diverting factory production from butter and bread to weapons and equipment. It also means prioritizing military supplies over civilian supplies. It is a measure we must take, albeit temporarily, if we are to prevail against our enemies.
strings.NTG_a_call_to_arms_desc:
When the October Revolution began, when our soldiers and sailors rose up to fight Kolchak and his cronies, the workers united in lockstep to overthrow the unpopular government and began to build our union by occupying vital junctions and donating to the military.

This civilian effort to strengthen their comrades in arms must be emulated, with volunteers and willing workers who will supply and assist the Red Army in its conquest of Siberia. Working together, we will be able to restore our Union, just like 1917.

Hence, we will announce a call to arms, with donations from workers to fund the Red Army and the collection of supplies and scrap metal to aid in the production of munitions.

With the help of civilians, the Red Army shall stand victorious!
strings.NTG_the_homefront_desc:
In warfare, there is a front that takes more precedence than any military plan, operation or action. Yet it is not on general orders, nor on maps. This front is known as the Homefront.

The Homefront is the most important aspect of any war. Failure to allocate proper resources here could be disastrous, and potentially bring about the end of our state, similar to the February and October Revolution that befell on the Tsarists and Kolchak during the First World War.

Should we want to win this war, we must have the people’s support. As the ones who produce the artillery shells and guns for our soldiers, who have to undergo severe rationing and expect enemy bombing and shelling in their villages and factories, their continued efforts ensure our soldiers can achieve victory.

Hence, we must inform them that their perseverance and efforts are essential to the war’s victory, and continue on in their roles in these tumultuous times.

To do this, the Presidium has commissioned the Agitprop Department to create propaganda posters and campaigns to bolster up the people’s support for the war, and ensure that the Homefront does not falter.
strings.NTG_restore_order_desc:
With the recent wars raging around us, and with some conflicts of our own, chaos has been widespread.

Many refugees are pouring in, trying to escape the conflict, while our border guards and militias are doing their best to make sure people are screened before entering the country. Our food situation could become dire if we continue to accept all these new refugees.

Besides this, the influx of people into our nation has led to some of our border towns and cities strained beyond control, whilst the potential for saboteurs to enter and cause havoc in our industries and fields remains very high, despite best efforts from our border officers.

We must restore order and control. The delegates have drafted a temporary measure to construct basic temporary shelters near major points of entry, while ensuring that only a certain number can enter the nation for the time being.
strings.NTG_over_valleys_over_mountains_desc:
Our social reforms have made us popular amongst our populace in Nizhny Tagil. Our working class no longer needs to slave through long working hours for meagre wages, and the average farmer does not need to worry about their daily bread.

This is a great achievement for us, and an ideal we want to spread across our region in our war for regional reunification.

With our army mobilised, and our men at the ready, we are ready to spread our ideals across the Siberian plains.

In the middle of Siberia's icy grip, the workers toil. Their spirits frozen, their dreams embroiled. Yet, the flame of socialism ignites their hearts anew as liberation dawns. Destiny's blessing has begun.

Over the valleys and over the mountains of Siberia, our red banner shall advance.
strings.NTG_for_trotskyism_desc:
As war and chaos rages all over Siberia, we have proven ourselves worthy of being the successors of Trotsky’s ideals. Through our extensive reforms to the economy and civilian industry, we have drastically improved the quality of life in our fledgling state. However, this is just the first step. Leon Trotsky advocated for such ideals to be spread across the world and as his torchbearer, we must bear the burden of spreading his ideals.

Hence, with the Red Army, we will show the workers across Siberia that we are fighting for the ideas of our founding fathers and a free worker's state, one untouched by degeneracy, where workers live healthily and happily without the fear of being abused or mistreated by the likes of capitalists and feudalistic overlords.

We shall fight for Trotskyism!
strings.NTG_for_the_motherland_desc:
The Rodina. Proud as it stood from the banks of the Dnieper all the way to Vladivostok. A bright shining red light across the world as a beacon of socialism that would shine across the globe.

However, the invasion by the Hitlerites and their cronies erased it from the maps and the global stage it once stood on. Her leaders abandoned her or used her for their own gain. Eventually she was broken up, shattered, and turned into a black slate encompassing the once proud lands.

We shall not let that injustice stand anymore. The Rodina was born into the hearts of every citizen who inhabits the lands of our former Soviet Union, and as its children, it is our duty to restore our motherland to the natural borders it inhabits.
strings.NTG_arise_fellow_russians_desc:
Whilst the importance of the revolution and Trotskyism as a whole is essential to our movement, another key factor is the Russian people.

Russians, likely the toughest and most experienced people of the past few centuries, still have the spirit to fight for their greatness, their freedom, their liberation. We survived the long tyranny of the tsars, the combat of the fiery years during the Civil War, the terror of the fascist invasion, the collapse of the Union, and now we, a new Smuta upon our broken lands. We no longer hold the mantle of the Motherland, leaving it open to reactionary elements who, given the chance, will almost certainly bring further terror upon the people. This cannot stand in any shape or form.

Hence forth, our socialist movement will emphasize the role of Russians in the realization of the revolutionary liberation of the Motherland. The message of uplifting the downtrodden Russians and fighting back against the Nazis shall be embedded within our framework as to recruit potential workers and soldiers to fight for our revolution.

Rest assured, that we will keep our messaging from getting too close to outright nationalism and ethnic supremacy. Nevertheless, the might of the Russian worker, peasant, and soldier will be highlighted as we march on.
strings.NTG_proletarians_of_the_world_rise_up: Proletarians of the World, Rise Up!
strings.NTG_proletarians_of_the_world_rise_up_de:
The Union was the prime example of a free worker's state and the closest we had ever come to liberating the loyal and hard-working people of the world, as we had the chance to spread our ideals across the 7 seas, dreaming of eliminating injustice and oppressive tyranny everywhere.

This dream was stolen away by the supporters of “Socialism in One Nation”, before the German war machine destroyed everything. The collapse of the Communist International led to empires and tyrannical states oppressing workers and proletarians without fear of revenge. No longer shall we stand this. We will not condone the deaths of our fellow workers at the hands of such murderers.

We will call all hands in the fields and factories everywhere to join us in the struggle for liberation. Instilling fear into the hearts of tyrants and hope into all workers across the world. Let us turn the cogs and call on the Proletarians of the World, the dawn of permanent revolution is close!

Proletarians of the World, Rise Up! Break the Chains that hold us down!
strings.NTG_for_it_is_our_duty_desc:
The unification of our region of Siberia is nearing by the day, whether we like it or not. Our enemies have built their army up and have prepared their war machines on our borders, ready to pounce the moment hostilities occur.

In these tumultuous and uncertain times, the duty of our citizens comes into importance. From the lowliest worker in the factory line to the elected delegates of the worker’s council, to the farmers who work on the collective farms, to our soldiers guarding our borders.

The nation has provided for them the benefits of their labour through their benefits, and in exchange, they shall provide the nation with their efforts to fight for the cause of socialism across Siberia.

The Union expects nothing less from its citizens, in their sacred duty to serve the nation with their role in society. It is of utmost importance, and each man, woman and child must be reminded of it.
strings.NTG_to_stand_and_fight_desc:
As of now, the Red Army has already successfully defended against our enemies actions, and have started their operation to liberate large swaths of territory formerly controlled by the likes of bourgeois dictatorships and feudal warlords.

They have fought valiantly, defending the bastion of socialism against those who seek to oppress and enslave us. They have chosen to fight on behalf of the nation, with valour and tenacity.

Our brave soldiers, with their ferocity in combat, are motivated as they were before the start of our Reunification Campaign of Central Siberia. They will stand and fight for the banner of equality and socialism, to be raised across all of the cities in Siberia, from Tomsk to Kansk!
strings.NTG_the_question_of_control_desc:
Ever since the proclamation of our commune, the many revanchists, capitalists and the false socialists that broke away during the chaos of the Central Siberian War have been looking at us like a piece of meat to be devoured.

Now, after an extensive reform to the army, industry and our society, it is now time to prove them wrong. However, there is one more thing we need to address. The fate of our foes.

Our newly conquered lands have to be properly integrated, to not only establish our administrative systems and exert control, but also prevent possible uprisings against our rule. This however also brings up the question, what shall be the fate of the former governments that we have defeated?

Sedov has asked the Central Committee of Nizhny Tagil what is necessary to ensure the party's ideals and governance, to ensure control over the region, as well as the fate of the defeated nations’ governments.

We must decide quickly, for the sake of stability during the war, should we want to succeed in securing our control over this region.
strings.NTG_a_necessary_evil_desc:
Within the former lands of the Union, there lies a cancer, a malevolent disease that has corrupted the minds of tens of thousands of Russians, and that is reactionary thinking.

This reactionary hydra is a monster we have yet to fully kill. Similar to the Greek legend, it has multiple heads. One head is the capitalist kleptocrats that have killed in the name for profit, the second is the head of fascism who kills in the name of purity, the third is the head of theocracy who kills in the name of corrupt deities, and the fourth is the head of monarchism that kills in the name of royalty.

This monster has cast a shadow over the Motherland, and it is our duty to strike down this corrupt beast before it claims more lives. To do so, security and pacification measures will be enforced across the commune, with Red Guard and rear guard battalions being deployed to patrol towns and cities with traces of reactionism, and eliminating any with extreme prejudice.

If we want to ensure a Union of prosperity, one where the worker and peasant can coexist without inequality and classism, we must institute necessary revolutionary terror to rid violent reactionaries.
strings.NTG_peace_over_violence_desc:
“If you are called upon to govern humans, treat them humanely”, a quote first spoken by comrade Mikhail Kalinin during the early days of the revolution, and one which still stays true to this day.

Unlike the Union’s earlier conquests during the Civil War, we are no longer in a state to be pillaging without concern as the lands have been ravaged by banditry. To show that we are better than the common bandit, we must cater and bring attention to the needs of the hundreds and thousands of new souls under the rule of our commune.

Henceforth, our Soviet code of conduct will explore and prioritize the need for peaceful means in both occupation and reintegration. The population of newly taken lands will no longer be at risk of pillaging or persecution, as we shall ensure that the Red Army is a force of revolutionary liberation rather than imperialist butchery.

This policy of peace over violence will be adhered to throughout the new Soviet Union, as we approach the question of regional reunification.
strings.NTG_law_and_order_desc:
After numerous experiences with anti-revolutionary terrorists within conquered lands, with some in our own commune in Nizhny Tagil, it has become clear that more extreme measures will need to be taken to fully rid the region of these anti-socialist cells.

Following much deliberation with the heads of the Red Army and Internal Affairs, Premier Sedov has announced the immediate implementation of several new security measures aimed at rooting out monarchist, bourgeois and reactionary elements from our communist society.

These include an increase in security spending, increased deployment of Army and police units in urban regions and state-wide mandatory curfews in areas of high anti-revolutionary activity.

These security measures are temporary, in order to stabilize our situation and ensure order is restored in these regions. The Presidium has promised the repeal of these measures once our enemies have been vanquished within Central Siberia.
strings.NTG_forgive_the_unforgiven_desc:
When it comes to the matter of political prisoners, our original policy for these anti-revolutionary criminals has been either imprisonment, penal labor, or even capital punishment.

However, due to the recent quadrupling of political prisoners held in custody due to our campaign to reclaim the Motherland, we will have to adopt a new method of pacification.

In a measure mostly supported by the reformists and moderates within the presidium, we shall begin a rehabilitation campaign for thousands of imprisoned soldiers and military officers of our recently conquered lands.

These rehabilitative practices will only be permitted for persons deemed appropriate, as to prevent any reactionaries and degenerates from enlisting in the ranks of the Red Army.

Many hardline delegates have objected to this order, claiming that this will open the door for degeneracy and reactionarism, which could corrupt and destroy the army. But their calls will fall on deaf ears. If we wish to forge a truly unbreakable Union, we must show compassion for our misguided comrades where we can and should.
strings.NTG_we_shall_fight_for_justice_desc:
As the Germans invaded our nation, and the subsequent power struggles and failure of the West Russian War, our Union plunged into anarchy. The same anarchy which we find ourselves in, roaming with bandits, oppressors and looters, whilst opportunistic warlords rose up, and carved out their own fiefdoms in the chaos.

The anarchy brought much injustice, at the hands of such bandits and looters in the chaos, whilst the other warlord states committed unspeakable crimes against the workers and peasants in their realm. These crimes are an attack against us all who live in Nizhny Tagil, and we shall tolerate it no longer.

We are stronger now, with our army and citizens alike, who are ready to fight for justice in these Siberian plains, to find those who are responsible for the crimes against the people.

Henceforth, we shall fight in defence of the workers who are being oppressed by the capitalists and their cronies! We shall fight against the opportunistic brigands who steal from our populace! We shall defend against those who dare desecrate the sacred might of the proletariat!

We shall fight for the People’s Justice!
strings.NTG_and_the_union_desc:
Fighting for the people’s justice is not the only thing the soldiers in our army fight for.

Many soldiers who serve in our Red Army are motivated by their willingness to protect their families and the place they call home, to ensure that their children or their spouses can lead a healthier and safer life under our flag, where everyone has more than enough to eat, warm clothes and a roof over their heads.

These ideals push many of our soldiers to stand up and fight for our commune’s cause. For their families, for a better tomorrow, for the lives they seek to pursue under our flag. These personal motivations will drive them to fight for the Union we seek to restore.

We have done it before in 1918 with their forefathers, and we shall do it again here and now with them.
strings.NTG_a_red_siberia_desc:
At long last, through the harsh winter storms, the vicious battles in the plains, alongside the horrors of conflict, we have valiantly crushed our enemies and have come to encompass the entirety of Central Siberia.

The cities are flying the flag of brilliant scarlet red once more, as our Red Army triumphs over the armies of the defeated states. We have returned back to where our forefathers started.

Now we must focus on the present and look towards an ambitious future, fixing our administrative systems and looking towards the lands in the Far East. Rebuilding and developing our newly taken lands, enacting the processes of healing and unity in our fight to restore our Union and consolidating our new rule over our republic, as Premier Sedov leads us to a new glorious beginning.

A bright future awaits us comrades! Long Live the Union! Long Live Premier Sedov!
strings.NTG_intro.1.d:
Lev sat at his desk, looking out the window over Nizhny Tagil. It had been almost ten years since his father had died, and even if he had been there, they would not have been easy. Lev Trotsky would be aghast at what had become of Russia, with reactionaries, fascist scum, and traitors to the revolution around every corner. His father would already have plans in motion of course, pushing the revolution ever onward.

How could they push global revolution while Russia lay in shambles? They couldn't even push Siberian revolution. Sedov remembered a distinct moment from his childhood, his father rushing around Moscow scrambling to align dozens of men and unions to back his plan before Bukharin, with little Lev in tow all the while. His father had an energy that the son had never felt he could match. Where organizing and direct action had energized Trotsky, it left Lev tired and overwhelmed.

But his father was right, it was paramount that socialism continue to stretch beyond the borders. In quiet moments, Lev the elder would rave about all the places socialism could be pushed on, Indochina and the Levant, Latin America and Britain and even Germany. The chairman rose from his seat, standing at the window and staring down at the streets, full of busy workers with scraps of red worn wherever they could be. Lev smiled sadly. His father might not be alive, and he might not be overjoyed at the state of Nizhny Tagil and Russia. But Lev would not allow him to be disappointed either.
strings.NTG_intro.2.d:
Sitting at his desk at the heart of Nizhny Tagil, Lev Sedov sat in solitude, lost in his thoughts as he mulled over the ideology of his father, his predecessor, Lev Trotsky. He reflected upon a time when the world was engulfed by the fascist menace, a time where his father’s ideas served as a beacon of hope for the oppressed masses. Trotsky’s last wishes were for Sedov to continue what he had started, and lead the revolution to new heights. With assistance from his loyal comrades, Sedov liberated Nizhny Tagil and began paving the way for a new era of peace and prosperity.

As the years passed, Sedov’s tireless efforts brought stability to the disorderly region, and implemented many of his father’s revolutionary ideas that he was unable to implement himself. Sedov, continued the permanent revolution, fighting tirelessly for the rights of workers and the downtrodden, and reaffirmed his commitment to a world revolution. Looking out over the city with a slight breeze blowing through his hair, Sedov knew that his father would be proud of what he had accomplished, the only legitimate revolution, the permanent revolution. He had carried the legacy of Trotskyism and turned theory into practice.

As the sun began to lower below the horizon, and night fell upon Nizhny Tagil, Sedov closed his eyes and breathed in the bitterly cold air. With the support of his comrades and the people of Nizhny Tagil, he would continue the fight for a continued revolution, carrying the torch of his father’s revolutionary spirit to the future.
strings.NTG_intro.3.d:
It was a nice yet dark night in Nizhny Tagil as Sedov took a few moments to look over the city he and his party had ruled over for years now, enjoying the breeze blowing past him. This age old city, one of the few grand cities of the motherland not engulfed by fascist flames, though it still held a cruel reality to it.

As much as Sedov had hoped it to be when he first arrived at Nizhny Tagil, he had to admit it to himself, the place was an absolute mess. No matter how many red banners were set up across the streets, no matter how many Trotskyist propaganda posters decorated the walls, the city was a gray and disappointing urban sector.

Yet Sedov still had hope, deep in his heart, hope that this city could be reforged by the fires of the proletariat, overcoming the warlord slums that surrounded it, it would become a beacon of the true revolution. To add on to this idealistic outcome, progress was being made with the recent economic reforms, now jobs were rising and poverty in the area was finally starting to wind down.

But Sedov still knew there was more to be done, he knew better than to be a naive bastard and think this was it. No, he knew there was more potential, more to be uncovered in this vast urban stretch, the revolution has yet to fully bring this city back to life. As the Soviets expand and march on the rest of those damned warlords, Nizhny Tagil shall be a bright shining beacon, a centerpoint of Soviet culture and a socialist utopia.

Though that was all for later, Sedov reminded himself, he had to think in the present and start building the bridges and roads to the end goal he had been envisioning. As he finished wrapping up his thoughts and began walking back to his office, he turned to look over his balcony one more time, overlooking the window lights sprinkled over the fields of concrete and steel, and saw a glorious future waiting ahead.
